used.how: the block path is judged on index SETS with ties at the 512th value counted apart (sorted score lists equal), never on positions
tie order of topk_large_indices is undefined: the test compares sets and verifies differences are 512th-value ties via the scores at both id lists
the glued path's block maxes are rolled with the same phase table as its scores before the block top-k (block_topk phase=), so tie order stays per alone chip row
every block-select op runs on the matmul grid (max_grid: 11x10), the compute sub-device of the gather-hide regions the top-k runs in
the packed check gives all four segment states one capacity (DS41-381)
test hooks set on the held instances' module globals as well as the current module (DS41-380)

missing: ttnn.gather's ROW_MAJOR kernel holds whole input rows in L1 per core (unusable for long-row block gathers): DS41-379
the score fork's block_max_out cannot write blocks wider than 8 keys (16-byte fp32 runs per tile row); a wider block needs a separate fold
ops a test or a model step adds beside the index top-k run inside a gather-hide region (sub-devices): only grid-limited ops work there (DS41-382)
the score fork's writer-core block max costs ~3-4x more in the glued lane_ranges ring than in the single ring (+1.3 vs +0.34 ms a layer at 139264): measured in tests/perf/test_bsel_score_probe.py

decisions taken autonomously and marked DECIDED in BREADCRUMBS (new block_select_ttnn ops instead of ttnn.gather; block 32; the length threshold INDEXER_BLOCK_SELECT_MIN with both paths warmed)
